title: Tutorial: KV cache reuse with llama-server (GitHub discussion #13606, llama.cpp), author smahs, 17 May 2025; maintainer ggerganov replies 19-20 May 2025; later comments to Aug 2026
setup: Tutorial model gemma-2-2b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf, llama-server -c 1024 -np 2 (2 slots x 512 ctx). Hardware not stated. 43-token prompt. Later user comment (Aug 2026): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL (a MoE), --cpu-moe, 8 threads, parallel 1, with a GPU offload setting, draft-mtp speculative decoding.

numbers.value: 1 (log: 'need to evaluate at least 1 token to generate logits', kv cache rm [42,end))

numbers.what: Aug 2026 user log, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE: cache hit
numbers.baseline: no cache: prompt_n 35, prompt_ms 541.462 (64.6 tok/s, 15.47 ms/token)
numbers.ratio: 4.86x less prompt time for 8.75x fewer tokens (per-pass fixed cost visible: 27.9 vs 15.5 ms/token)

numbers.where: same; after restart restore did not give cache hits (cache_n 0) - unresolved bug report

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: Common-prefix check skips prefill for the matching part
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: Matches the logs (kv cache rm [n_past,end)). But slot selection is by similarity threshold -sps default 0.5, not a strict LCP rule; an LCP claim appears only in a Mar 2026 user comment ('picks a sufficient match based on LCP similarity rather than the optimal one').

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: Nothing there triggers on keystrokes
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: Correct; no trigger or streaming-input feature exists in the thread.

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: First pass: model/hardware not stated
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: Model IS stated: gemma-2-2b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf (-c 1024 -np 2). Hardware is not stated.

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: First pass: slot save 72 tokens 1.4 ms, restore 0.74 ms
First pass: 43-token repeat re-evaluates 1 token; -sps default 0.5
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: as above

why: Mechanism (exact-prefix KV reuse on the CPU side) transfers fully: it is host-independent and costs no decode time. It does not trigger on typing, and does not change decode tok/s, which is the only thing our regime (NVMe-streamed experts, batch 1) is bound by. The MoE log shows prefill of 4 tokens still costs 111 ms (27.9 ms/token vs 15.5 ms/token for 35), i.e. a small partial pass is not proportionally cheap, which is consistent with our finding that chunk passes re-read expert bytes.
quality_loss: None (exact reuse). Caveat from maintainer: SWA models (Gemma 2/3) need --swa-full for some of the techniques once context exceeds the window (1024 for Gemma).
limitations: Author: -sps 'doesn't always behave predictably, inconsistent and unexpected slot switching'; --slots was flagged unsafe by ggerganov (19 May 2025; a Jan 2026 comment says it is now enabled by default). Cyclic N+1 prompts over N slots never hit (ExtReMLapin, 24 May 2025).
contradicts_our_findings: No. Supports F.md family 22: exact-prefix reuse exists; nothing triggers on keystrokes.

title: server : host-memory prompt caching (llama.cpp PR #16391), Georgi Gerganov; created 2025-10-02, merged 2025-10-09 into master (GitHub API: state closed, merged true, +809/-467, base master)
setup: No benchmark. Description: host-RAM prompt cache acting as 'extra slots'; prefix similarity decides hot-swap into llama_context if it reduces processing. Limits: --cache-ram/-cram (MiB) and max cached tokens (default = --context-size). -cram -1 = no limit, 0 = disabled. Context checkpoints default raised 3 to 8. Works for dense, MoE, SWA, SSM per maintainer comment; incompatible with mtmd (multimodal) at this version.

why: CPU-side RAM mechanism, model independent. But its cost is host RAM: 0.36 MiB/token for the large model in the log, so a 4k-token conversation is ~1.4 GiB, which competes with the expert cache at 8/16 GB and the default 8 GiB limit would need lowering. Saves prefill only, never decode.

why: GPU serving, many concurrent requests, goal = stop prefill from stalling other users' decodes (generation stalls). Single user batch-1 CPU with NVMe-bound experts has no decode to protect; the paper itself says chunks are 'somewhat slower than full prefills' and raise TTFT. It supports our finding that chunking costs extra passes; on our regime each pass re-reads experts so cost is far above the 25% here.
ablation: Yes: Table 4 separates hybrid batching vs chunked prefill vs both; Fig 14 chunk-size overhead.
limitations: Authors: smaller chunks reduce efficiency (arithmetic intensity, repeated KV reads); disaggregated prefill/decode compared only qualitatively (left to future work).
contradicts_our_findings: No; consistent with F.md note that chunking gives higher average TTFT.

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: 9,305.3 vs 847.5 (decode config BS=4/SL=2048, m=10) - ratio 10.98x

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: 8x = Qwen-MoE vs Llama-1B, 11x = OLMoE vs Llama-1B; vs Llama-3B the ratios are 4.4-6.1x. The paper's own wording is 'dense models of comparable active parameter count'.

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: Sec VI

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: First pass: launches/token measured in prefill
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: The 9,305 figure is a decode-config figure (m=10); prefill has 13,741 kernels for a 512-token forward pass, a different quantity.

why: GPU eager-mode PyTorch launch path (single-threaded Python+CUDA dispatch, ~4.7 us/kernel floor). Does not exist in llama.cpp CPU graph execution. The high kernel count comes from HF-style routing and per-expert loops, an implementation artefact; the paper itself says the main levers are reducing kernel count or amortising submission (e.g. CUDA graphs).
ablation: Cross-platform H100 vs H200 CPU comparison; eager vs FlashAttention-2 (Fig 9). No fusion/CUDA-graph ablation.
limitations: Authors: NVIDIA only, depends on CUDA tracing, replay-based attribution imperfect for dynamic/autotuned kernels; HDBI is a diagnostic ratio; effect weakens as HDBI rises above ~0.3.
contradicts_our_findings: No. It says nothing about CPU inference. It does say additional cores give no benefit for the dispatch path, which is a GPU single-thread issue.

Baseline Default synchronous deployment DP8-TP4-EP32 on 32 dies; ASAP DP4-TP4-EP16 (same device count); also ChunkedPrefill baseline. Poisson arrivals, Huawei Cloud production trace lengths <=32k.

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: +90% is vs ChunkedPrefill (20 vs 10.5 RPS); vs Default it is +194% (20 vs 6.8).

why: Datacentre NPU with 32-NPU expert parallelism and a host-launch model; the dispatch bubble (220 us x 61 layers = 13.4 ms) matters because TTFT is ~350 ms. It contributes +6% of throughput, i.e. it is the smallest of ASAP's four optimisations, and even on this NPU it is a few percent. In our regime a layer step costs hundreds of ms of disk time, so 220 us is invisible.
ablation: Yes: Sec 5.5: triple-stream overlap +12.4%, bubble-free dispatch +6% and 13 ms TTFT; other components in 5.5.1 (not itemised here).
limitations: Not stated in a dedicated section in the text read; evaluated only on CloudMatrix384 and DeepSeek-V3.2.
contradicts_our_findings: No; it is a second published point (NPU host launch 220 us per layer, +6% throughput) that per-layer dispatch removal is worth single-digit percent.
